images.prompt: A quiet mountain valley with an old thatched watermill beside a stream, just after sunset. The valley is a small, quiet mountain valley in rural Japan in late summer. A clear shallow stream runs over smooth rounded stones from the lower left foreground into the middle distance, between low banks of soft short green grass and clover. On the far bank, right of centre in the middle distance, stands one small old watermill hut with a thick, steep thatched roof and weathered dark wooden walls, and beside it a large wooden water wheel dips into the stream. Low rounded wooded hills close the valley on both sides and behind, so there is no far view: no distant snowy mountains, no sea, no lake, no far horizon. A single wild Japanese hare (nousagi: brown-grey fur, long upright ears with dark tips, lean body, a wild animal, not a white rabbit, not a pet rabbit, not a cartoon) belongs to this valley and lives on the near bank. The watermill is the only building: no houses, no temples, no shrines, no torii, no stone lanterns, no lanterns, no bridges, no fences, no steps, no boats, no people, no other animals, no birds. No pampas grass, no susuki, no bush clover, no bamboo, no maple leaves, no autumn colours, no persimmons, no rice paddies, no snow, no cherry blossoms, no plum blossoms, no camellias. The sun has just set behind the hills out of frame to the left: the sky above the hills is a soft gradated wash from warm apricot low down to rose and pale violet above, and the stream reflects these colours in long soft bands. The thatched roof of the mill catches the last warm light on its edge. The hare sits quietly on the near bank in the lower right, small in the frame, ears up, facing the stream. No moon yet. Apricot, rose, pale violet, soft grass green, warm brown thatch, cool grey-blue shadow under the banks. Japanese shin-hanga woodblock print in the manner of the 1920s-30s revival: flat layered areas of colour, visible woodgrain in the flat passages, softly gradated sky (bokashi), Western perspective and cast light held inside Japanese printmaking. The hills, the grass, the water, the mill and the hare are drawn as part of the print, in the same flat woodblock manner, never photographic. Calm, no people, no figures. Strong clear difference between the light and dark masses so the image still reads when reduced to a thumbnail. No text, no signature, no seal stamp, no lettering of any kind. No modern objects: no power lines, no utility poles, no electric lamps, no vehicles, no plastic, no road markings. Wide 16:9 landscape. Exposed so that texture is clearly visible everywhere. Shadows are lifted and open, full of visible detail, nothing crushed to pure black. High dynamic range, rich texture even in the darkest areas.
images.visual_review: Warm apricot and rose dusk, no moon. Stream enters from lower left; one thatched watermill is right of centre, one brown-grey long-eared wild hare sits at lower right. Shin-hanga-style textured colour areas; no people, other animals or lettering seen.
